findings.reason: The source-factored definition cites def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness, whose actual definition covers scalar functions on subsets of R; the two tube lemmas also cite thm-algebra-of-derivatives, whose actual theorem is one-dimensional. These do not supply multivariable C² regularity or the product and quotient rules used for rates and matrices on U⊂R^m. Use def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables and provide the needed multivariable product/reciprocal calculations (thm-chain-sum-product-and-composition-rules-for-banach-derivatives supplies the bounded-bilinear product rule). Also change “smooth extension” in thm-zero-compatible-modified-patankar-euler-admissibility to C²: only C² factors are assumed.

The PDS definition permits an arbitrary Ω, but alg-modified-patankar-euler and alg-mprk22-1 admit any nonnegative or positive input without requiring rates to be defined there; MPRK also evaluates rates at its stage z. For example, take Ω a small positive neighborhood of (1,1), p₂₁=d₁₂=10y₁, yⁿ=(1,1), and h=1. The Patankar stage is z=(1/11,21/11), outside Ω, so the MPRK rate evaluation p₂₁(z) is undefined. Make rate availability on all nonnegative states explicit, with local open extensions where smooth analysis needs them, or restrict the algorithms and theorem hypotheses to cover every required evaluation.

alg-zero-compatible-modified-patankar-euler and alg-mprk22-1 identify inadmissible inputs but do not specify the returned status for them. Add an explicit inadmissible-input branch before rate evaluation or linear solves; the modified Patankar Euler algorithm already specifies this branch.
